claude.sample_unit: LLM-generated mass casualty simulation scenarios (62 simulated patients), plus 2 public control scenarios

links.outcome: SSET score of LLM-generated scenarios before vs after expert human review and revision
links.effect: Median SSET rose from 78.5 (IQR 74-82) pre-revision to 94 (IQR 93-96) post-revision, matching public scenarios at 94 (IQR 93-95); review ~25 min per scenario.
links.quote: Upon re-evaluation post-revision, the AI-generated scenarios exhibited a marked improvement, achieving a median SSET score of 94 (IQR 93–96) across scenarios, compared to the scores of existing, publicly available mass casualty incident (MCI) scenarios.

links.outcome: Interrater reliability (ICC) of blinded ATLS-certified raters scoring scenarios
links.effect: ICC 0.965 for pre-revision AI scenarios, 1.00 (abstract) or 0.667 (results) for public scenarios, and 0.7425 post-revision, showing moderate to high agreement that varied across conditions.
links.quote: The interrater reliability, assessed through ICC, indicated moderate reliability for the post-revision scenarios (0.7425).

links.effect: Initial LLM scenarios scored 78.5 (IQR 74-82), lower than public scenarios at 94 (IQR 93-95).
links.quote: The initial LLM-generated scenarios demonstrated a median SSET score of 78.5 (IQR 74-82), substantially lower than the median score of 94 (IQR 93-95) observed in publicly available scenarios.

links.effect: After secondary human revision, median SSET improved to 94 (IQR 93-96), ICC 0.7425.
links.quote: Following secondary human revision and iterative refinement, the LLM-generated scenarios improved, achieving a median SSET score of 94 (IQR 93-96) with an interrater reliability ICC of 0.7425.
